components.cost_effect: One gradient evaluation and one LMO per update; neither is counted as the other.
components.goal: Select a feasible descent direction without projection.
components.key_estimate: With g(x)=max_{s in D}<x-s,grad f(x)>, the chosen direction satisfies <s-x,grad f(x)>=-g(x), and convexity gives f(x)-min_D f<=g(x).
components.name: Exact linear minimization
components.operation: Query grad f(x), then minimize its inner product over D and move along the feasible segment.
components.requires: Exact gradient and exact LMO over the same domain D.
transfer_checks: Approximate gradient or LMO errors require a separate error analysis.
Changing the domain or objective requires checking finite curvature.
A support bound requires atomic LMO outputs; arbitrary minimizers need not be vertices.

limitations.statement: Primal convergence holds with arbitrary exact minimizers, but sparse coordinate support is not guaranteed if the LMO returns dense minimizers. Atomic sparsity statements require an explicit atom-returning realization and suitable representation accounting.
This record does not establish an unrestricted Oracle Complexity Lower Bound or a runtime bound for arbitrary exact LMO implementations.

variants.cost: K exact gradient evaluations and K exact LMO calls, charged separately. Also charge K convex-combination updates and initialization/storage costs; implementation-specific gradient and LMO runtimes are not bounded here. No function-value evaluations or line searches are required by this variant. In a dense finite-dimensional representation each update uses O(n) arithmetic and the state/direction use O(n) storage, excluding oracle internals.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Supplementary PDF page 1 Algorithm 1; page 4 Theorem 1, delta=0.
variants.name: Algorithm 1: exact LMO and fixed step sizes
variants.output: Return the final feasible iterate x_K. Convention: K counts updates. The source pseudocode instead writes t=0,...,K inclusively, which produces x_{K+1}.
public_inputs: A feasible initial point x_0, access to the exact gradient and exact LMO over D, and an integer update budget K>=1.
variants.query_and_update: For t=0,...,K-1, obtain d_t=grad f(x_t), choose any s_t in argmin_{s in D}<s,d_t>, set gamma_t=2/(t+2), and update x_{t+1}=(1-gamma_t)x_t+gamma_t s_t. Convexity of D preserves feasibility. Ties may be resolved arbitrarily for primal performance.
variants.requirements: D is a nonempty compact convex subset of R^n, n>=1; f is convex and continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of D. Exact gradient and exact LMO access are available. The linked performance additionally requires finite curvature C_f as defined in the linked Theorem.
variants.state_and_initialization: Initialize x_0 in D. No vertex initialization is required for primal convergence.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Return after K updates. Fixed step sizes require neither C_f nor a Lipschitz constant as input. If a verified upper bound C_bar>=C_f is available, choose any integer K>=1 with 2 C_bar/(K+2)<=epsilon for the linked primal guarantee. This record does not add an adaptive gap stopping rule.
